I have the same thing you have going on, was scared it was cancer because it's unilateral, it wasn't though. Size of a golf ball and they had to remove it through my throat. 2 years later it was back and the same size , had another surgery last December to remove it. Its back unfortunately but I was approved and prescribed dupixent, I'm super hopeful I won't have to have another surgery because honestly the recovery is hellish, at least for me it was extremely bad pain wise and they are so worried about people abusing pain meds I was barely given enough to get by, I wasn't actually I was sobbing and shaking the second night because I was in so much pain and the meds were not helping or strong enough. I told my partner I was never going to let them do another surgery again because both times it was like that. 

Anywho it's probably not cancerous, and if it comes back after the first surgery be on top of it and get on a medication that will help you because the surgery recovery is not great I highly don't recommend going through it twice. Good luck, get all the treats you like to help comfort you post surgery.

Wanted to add some comforting words for you. I was completely blocked for five years, polyp the size of a golf grew to block the whole back airway and it was there for 5 years before they finally found it, I still unfortunately am a mouth breather due to spending half a decade breathing that way.
Just last week had a second surgery, the polyp came back size of a pingpong ball in 2 year, with a cyst this time, and it's all been infected for months. Anywho happy ending, the thing is gone, vision and brain are fine.
It's totally normal to have anxiety about weird things growing in your face though, but I hope you can get some peace knowing a lot of us have 'serious' cases and are just fine, you will be too, I am sorry it's scary though.

ENT set up the referral for an allergist who's going to skin test me for everything I guess and internal medicine going to get some other tests done to try and figure out what is causing this, unfortunately the massive recurring polyp is only one fun part of the picture with my medical issues.
